Cardiac Catheterization - 10/14/2026 - PED VAR

PROCEDURE INFORMATION
Operator: Dr. Karandeep Singh, Interventional Cardiologist
Location: St. John's Hospital
Indication: Ongoing angina with prior coronary artery bypass grafting requiring native coronary and bypass graft angiography
Contrast: 
Fluoroscopy time: 

PROCEDURE
Right femoral artery access was obtained for native coronary and bypass graft angiography. A JL4 catheter and JR 3.5 catheter were used to access the native coronary arteries and bypass grafts. Angiography demonstrated severe distal left main disease extending into the LAD and left circumflex systems. The LAD territory is revascularized by a LIMA to LAD graft. The left circumflex territory is unrevascularized with high-grade disease involving the distal AV groove branch and ostial obtuse marginal bifurcation lesion. The right coronary artery has diffuse in-stent restenosis, especially in the distal-mid RCA. Perclose was used for hemostasis.

Technical note: JL4 and JR 3.5 were the only two catheters needed for coronary and bypass graft angiography.

ACCESS
Right femoral artery
Sheath size: Not Provided
Closure: Perclose

CPT CODE
93459 - Right and left heart catheterization with coronary angiography and bypass graft angiography

PROCEDURAL SUMMARY
- Severe heavily calcified distal left main disease, approximately 90%, extending into both the LAD and left circumflex.
- LAD territory is revascularized by a widely patent LIMA to LAD graft with 60-70% touchdown stenosis and mild post-stenotic dilatation.
- Left circumflex territory is unrevascularized with high-grade bifurcation disease involving the distal AV groove branch and ostial OM branch; staged revascularization will be needed due to ongoing angina.

DETAILED PROCEDURAL SUMMARY
Right femoral artery access was obtained for native coronary and bypass graft angiography. JL4 and JR 3.5 catheters were the only catheters required. The left main is heavily calcified with severe distal disease in the range of 90%, extending into both the LAD and left circumflex. The LAD territory is revascularized by the LIMA to LAD graft. The LIMA to LAD is widely patent except for a 60-70% touchdown stenosis with mild post-stenotic dilatation. The left circumflex territory is unrevascularized with high-grade downstream disease in the AV groove branch as well as a 90% ostial obtuse marginal branch lesion, representing a bifurcation lesion. The OM vein graft is occluded. This territory will require staged revascularization of the OM and distal AV groove branch bifurcation because of ongoing angina. The right coronary artery has diffuse in-stent restenosis, especially in the distal-mid RCA, with maximum stenosis of approximately 60%. The RCA can be investigated further if revascularization of the culprit left circumflex system does not relieve symptoms. Perclose was used for hemostasis.

CORONARY ANATOMY
1. Dominance: Not Provided
2. Left Main: Heavily calcified distal left main disease approximately 90%, extending into both the LAD and left circumflex.
3. LAD: Severe disease involving the distal left main extension into the LAD; LAD territory revascularized by LIMA to LAD.
4. Diagonal: Not Provided
5. Ramus Intermedius: Not present.
6. Circumflex (LCX): Unrevascularized territory with high-grade downstream disease in the AV groove branch.
7. Obtuse Marginal (OM): 90% ostial OM branch lesion at a bifurcation; OM vein graft is occluded.
8. RCA: Diffuse in-stent restenosis, especially in the distal-mid RCA, maximum approximately 60%.
9. Posterolateral (PL): Not Provided
10. PDA: Not Provided

BYPASS GRAFTS
- LIMA to LAD: Widely patent except for a 60-70% touchdown stenosis with mild post-stenotic dilatation.
- OM vein graft: Occluded.

IMPRESSION
1. Severe heavily calcified distal left main coronary artery disease, approximately 90%, extending into the LAD and left circumflex.
2. Patent LIMA to LAD with 60-70% touchdown stenosis and mild post-stenotic dilatation.
3. Unrevascularized left circumflex territory with high-grade AV groove branch disease and 90% ostial OM bifurcation lesion, with occluded OM vein graft.
4. Diffuse RCA in-stent restenosis, most prominent in the distal-mid RCA, maximum approximately 60%.
5. Staged revascularization of the OM and distal AV groove bifurcation is planned because of ongoing angina; RCA can be investigated if left circumflex revascularization does not relieve symptoms.
